question: Can one pre-training recipe be universally effective across supervised, few-shot and generation tasks, independent of the architecture choice?
hypothesis: Diverse denoising objectives mixed in pre-training (plus mode tokens) give a better trade-off than span corruption (T5) or causal LM (GPT-like) alone; the objective matters more than the backbone.
contributions: Mixture-of-Denoisers (R, S, X denoisers) pre-training objective
Mode switching: paradigm tokens in pre-training and downstream use
Architecture-agnostic framework; ablations on decoder-only vs encoder-decoder
Scaling to 20B parameters with SOTA on 50+ supervised tasks, strong zero/one-shot and CoT; release of UL2 20B and Flan-UL2 20B checkpoints

method.summary: Pre-train models on C4 with a mixture of 7 span-corruption denoisers (R: short spans, low corruption; S: prefix-LM; X: extreme long spans or high corruption), each prefixed with a mode token. Compare against CLM, PrefixLM, SC (T5), SCLM and UniLM objectives on decoder-only and encoder-decoder backbones at ~167M/335M, then scale to 1B/0.5T tokens and 20B/1T tokens.
method.task: Self-supervised pre-training (denoising / inputs-to-targets), then supervised finetuning and prompt-based in-context evaluation

training.objective: Mixture of 7 denoisers (Table 1): R (mu=3,r=0.15),(mu=8,r=0.15); S (mu=L/4,r=0.25,n=1); X (mu=3,r=0.5),(mu=8,r=0.5),(mu=64,r=0.15),(mu=64,r=0.5); equal participation; mode token [R]/[S]/[X] prepended
training.optimizer: Adafactor (pretraining); finetuning Adafactor with reset states and/or loss normalized by real target tokens
training.lr: pretraining: inverse square root (value not stated); finetuning {5e-5, 1e-5, 1e-4}
training.hardware: 64 to 128 TPUv4 chips per ablation run; 512 TPUv4 chips for 20B

other.loss_spikes: occasional loss spikes in 20B run, no mitigation
other.finetune_protocol: continuous finetuning from checkpoints every 50k to 100k steps; per-task, not co-trained (some exceptions in appendix); stop once SOTA
